title: MFA fatigue at 7:03 a.m.
scenario: You wake to six MFA prompts for your work account. A Teams message from “IT” says the prompts are part of a security test and asks you to approve the next one to stop the notifications.

answers.A: Deny all prompts, contact IT/security through the official channel, and change credentials if compromise is suspected.
answers.B: Use the account security page to review sessions and revoke unknown access before calling IT.
answers.C: Approve once to stop the prompts, then change the password immediately.

explanation: MFA fatigue attacks rely on annoyance and timing. Approval gives the access the attacker is repeatedly requesting.
proTip: Annoyance is a pressure tactic, not proof.
